title: Unhandled MusicKit play() rejection after a mid-track Apple start
acceptance: No Unhandled Promise Rejection "The play() method was called without a previous stop() or pause() call." appears during timeline taps, drags or Next on iPhone Safari.
Any play() rejection on a superseded or re-cued start is caught and recorded in the timing log, not surfaced as unhandled.
An adapter test covers the re-cue path (set-queue-start (again)) rejecting.
nextAction: Reproduce first with a timeline drag (the two rejections came at the start and end of one drag, #15 and #32), then with discrete mid-track taps. Trace the mid-track re-cue in apps/web/src/lib/playback/apple-music-adapter.ts (prepare cues the window start, the pre-play seek dirties the cue, play() re-queues at the entered position) and find the play() call whose promise is not handled. Agent-created: Backlog until the owner sets Ready.

evidence.summary: Owner's iPhone Safari run on production af800c8 (Worker d05bb48f, SPA assets/index-ChxMwIpX.js), 2026-11-03 about 13:28-13:58 MST, ?playback-timing=1, class [QA] Audit Experienced Cycle (24 Apple Music tracks); console read by the Air conductor through Safari Web Inspector, plus the owner's screen recordings. Three unhandled rejections in the run. Two came right after starts that logged set-queue-start (again) (#15, the first start of one continuous timeline drag, and #32, its last; the drag ran #15-#32, 18 starts); the third followed #67, whose lines were not visible. None followed a Next start. No user-visible effect seen.
Mid-track entry re-cues with a second setQueue before play (see #669 note 8).
#717 final review finding 5: trigger was a drag, not discrete jumps; corrected here.
